name: Nezzar and Binary String
description: Nezzar has a binary string $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$ that he wants to share with his best friend, Nanako. Nanako will spend $$$q$$$ days inspecting the binary string. At the same time, Nezzar wants to change the string $$$s$$$ into string $$$f$$$ during these $$$q$$$ days, because it looks better. It is known that Nanako loves consistency so much. On the $$$i$$$-th day, Nanako will inspect a segment of string $$$s$$$ from position $$$l_i$$$ to position $$$r_i$$$ inclusive. If the segment contains both characters ' 0 ' and ' 1 ', Nanako becomes unhappy and throws away the string. After this inspection, at the $$$i$$$-th night, Nezzar can secretly change strictly less than half of the characters in the segment from $$$l_i$$$ to $$$r_i$$$ inclusive, otherwise the change will be too obvious. Now Nezzar wonders, if it is possible to avoid Nanako being unhappy and at the same time have the string become equal to the string $$$f$$$ at the end of these $$$q$$$ days and nights.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n,q$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$0 \le q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line of each test case contains a binary string $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$. The third line of each test case contains a binary string $$$f$$$ of length $$$n$$$. Then $$$q$$$ lines follow, $$$i$$$-th of them contains two integers $$$l_i,r_i$$$ ($$$1 \le l_i \le r_i \le n$$$)  — bounds of the segment, that Nanako will inspect on the $$$i$$$-th day. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ for all test cases doesn't exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$, and the sum of $$$q$$$ for all test cases doesn't exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print " YES " on the single line if it is possible to avoid Nanako being unhappy and have the string $$$f$$$ at the end of $$$q$$$ days and nights. Otherwise, print " NO ". You can print each letter in any case (upper or lower).
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1477B — Nezzar and Binary String [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
